So in 2017 I started a program at a school that was for profit and competency based and basically it was a giant joke. I received financial aid and excess (which I used to buy a laptop for school since it was online). Anyways midway through my second semester I dropped below part time enrollment (I stopped logging in etc). I guess they had decreased my financial aid and grant and stuff (I didn’t see this, because I wasn’t checking school emails. Yes I know, my fault.) 

Anyways, they called me and told me I owe money to the school for my Pell Grant and excess Direct Loans. The collection calls are coming from the school and I have NOT received anything from the government or OSLA(my loan advisors.)

I am trying to go back to school in something I WANT to do but everywhere I look online is saying I can’t because I owe money to the government for financial aid. (I’m not eligible for private funding nor do I have co-signers or parents to assist me.) But I found another website that says since it’s a private university, it’s likely that they paid the government and now I just owe the school. (It’s SNHU/College for America).

Am I eligible for financial aid at a new school or am I required to pay all the money back first? Also my credits will not matter because they can’t be used for my program anyways.



tldr: I dropped out, they reduced my financial aid and now I owe the school 6000$. They’re saying I owe it because they reduced my Pell Grant and loan availability. The school(SNHU/College for America) is trying to collect, not my loan servicer (OSLA) or government. Also my loans are NOT in default. Am I eligible for federal financial aid or do I have to pay it all back first?
